ai.description: *Theloderma nagalandense* is a small treefrog (approx. 30 mm). It features a dark brown dorsum with irregular, raised tubercles and a creamy-white venter. Distinctive traits include extensive webbing.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Theloderma nagalandense* is best distinguished by the presence of numerous prominent, conical tubercles on its dorsum, which are significantly more dense than in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Theloderma nagalandense* inhabits subtropical evergreen forests in the Nagaland region, typically found at elevations ranging from 1,200 to 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Nagaland Treefrog is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged against mossy surfaces during the day to avoid predators before emerging to forage at night.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Theloderma nagalandense* breeds in tree holes during the monsoon season (June–August), depositing small clutches of eggs in water-filled cavities.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Theloderma nagalandense* is endemic to the high-altitude forests of Nagaland, India, specifically recorded in the Phek district at elevations around 1,500–1,800 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Nagaland Treefrog emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "tink" notes, typically heard calling from vegetation near small forest pools or streams.
